tickets.title: Baseline and self-audit
tickets.reason: Know the true starting state before changing anything.
tickets.goal: Run the full gate, `brain doctor`, `brain lint`, `brain hr audit`, `brain lint --transcript`; consolidate the pending inbox (`brain learn consolidate`, the first real delta) and check `brain learn verify`; record every number in docs/BUILD_STATUS.md under a new dated heading.
tickets.accept: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . && python3 bin/brain doctor && python3 bin/brain lint && python3 bin/brain hr audit
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: Live platform checks that a one-repo session can do
tickets.reason: Several design choices rest on platform behaviour nobody has measured.
tickets.goal: In this one-repo session: do the brain's hooks in .claude/settings.json fire (guard_paths on an edit to memory/, session_end at stop)? Do a skill's frontmatter hooks fire? Do helpers honour model, effort and omitClaudeMd (read each helper's model from `brain ledger` and its transcript)? Does changing effort mid-session keep the prompt cache (compare cache-read share before and after with `brain ledger`)? Record each as a dated fact through `brain learn note --trust external` only where an official page confirms it; otherwise record the observation in docs/BUILD_STATUS.md.
tickets.accept: grep -q 'CB-201' docs/BUILD_STATUS.md
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: End-to-end trial on a scratch project with real helpers
tickets.reason: Everything so far was proven by scripts; nothing has been run as a real two-repo flow.
tickets.goal: Create a scratch project under the session scratchpad (git init with a local bare remote), then run the real flow as the lead: boot (bootstrap), init, requirements ledger for a small but real app or document, plan and `brain hr staff`, hire two or three helpers through `brain hr hire`, settle, gate, release, checkpoint, resume, handover, close. Note every place the instructions, skills or commands were unclear, slow or wrong; fix each in the brain with a test; record tokens and minutes from `brain ledger`.
tickets.accept: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . && python3 bin/brain lint
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: A/A run, then the first paired evaluation of HR templates
tickets.reason: No one knows yet whether a template brief beats a plain brief; the rack's worth is unproven.
tickets.goal: Pre-register with `brain eval prereg` before any run. First an A/A run (same arm twice) on the 8 dev tasks in evals/tasks to measure noise. Then template brief versus plain brief (`brain hr hire` with and without `--template`) on the dev tasks, graded by `brain eval grade`, compared with `brain eval compare`. Report the verdict in the brain's own wording (ship, revert, not proven) with n. Do not touch the 4 held-out tasks while tuning.
tickets.accept: python3 bin/brain eval audit && ls evals/prereg/*.json
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: Selection: raise held-out accuracy honestly
tickets.reason: The right template is in the top three for 86% of held-out requests; one in seven misses.
tickets.goal: Write a NEW held-out set of 100 requests (evals/hr_golden_2.jsonl) before changing anything, measure, then improve `hr.select` (candidates: character n-gram overlap for typos and Spanish inflection, a small synonym table built only from dev misses, field weights) using dev and the old set only. Report old and new accuracy on the new held-out set; keep a change only if top-3 rises by at least 3 points there.
tickets.accept: python3 -m unittest tests.test_hr && python3 bin/brain hr audit
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: Template quality pass
tickets.reason: Templates were written from research but never read side by side or tried.
tickets.goal: A fresh-context reviewer reads all 100 templates against hr/GUIDELINES.md and docs/research/round3/04-domain-methods.md and lists: job titles with generic advice, method lines with no reason, base agents whose tools cannot do the method, unsourced numbers, near-duplicate pairs. Fix what is confirmed. The five data templates with thin sourcing (biodiversity, ML experiments, RAG index, spreadsheets, statistics) get a short research pass first.
tickets.accept: python3 bin/brain hr audit && python3 -m unittest tests.test_hr
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: Open review items
tickets.reason: Small defects left from the two reviews.
tickets.goal: Work the lists under 'Open, with reasons' and 'Open for HR' in docs/BUILD_STATUS.md: success output that mixes streams, repo map listing generated files, radar thread shutdown time (measure it), tunables still inline, lead-record field names, radar state dirtying the tree daily, `staff` parallel default, forged inbox records, a use for the scout tier. Each fix gets a test.
tickets.accept: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . && python3 bin/brain lint
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: Research round four
tickets.reason: Model and platform facts age; some areas were researched only from search summaries.
tickets.goal: Run `brain radar --force` and handle its official leads. Re-verify every fact in memory/facts.jsonl and memory/models.json against its source page. Research, with the brain's researcher agent and sources, the areas earlier memos marked as unverified: persona effects on current Claude models, whether a pointer-to-file brief costs or saves tokens (measure it with the ledger in CB-202), skill description budgets, effort and cache behaviour. At most four researchers at once. Record confirmed facts through the learning pipeline.
tickets.accept: test -d docs/research/round4
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: Red team and final independent review
tickets.reason: The author of a fix is the worst judge of it.
tickets.goal: One redteam pass on the whole design (what would make this brain harmful or useless over a year of use?) and one fresh-context review against docs/EXECUTION_PLAN.md section 1 and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, both with reproductions. Fix every blocking and should-fix finding with a test.
tickets.accept: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . && python3 bin/brain doctor && python3 bin/brain lint && python3 bin/brain hr audit
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

tickets.title: Close out
tickets.reason: The owner reads three files; they must be true.
tickets.goal: Update docs/BUILD_STATUS.md, docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, NEEDS_YOU.md and OWNER_GUIDE.md to what is now true, mark tickets, checkpoint, `brain close`, push. State plainly what is still unproven.
tickets.accept: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . && python3 bin/brain lint
tickets.return: at most 250 words: what changed, the acceptance command and its result line, anything that differs from the brief

Do a skill's own frontmatter hooks fire after it is used? Record either way
Push to both repos from one session with branch protection on the brain's main
